chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Small groups and the trio's big-band sound
summary: With Candy on drums and organ, the trio sounded like a big band.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: So now we go from where?
Well, into the latter half of the Sixties and into the Seventies.

Well, Joe and I worked quite a bit with that small group. We played, like, Lennie's up in Boston, and we played several other places, like... Oh, it's so hard to think of the places... I played out there on the Island...
Well, it's not so important to remember the specific places as much as which bands or which combos you had -- not necessarily where you played.

Mmm-hmm. Well, the combos that I had turned out pretty good, because when Candy was with the trio we could sound like a big band or we could sound like a small band -- which was very good for us. Because we only need... There was only three people, and we could fill up the organ

with the chords and so forth, so we could play arrangements just like a big band would play. So it was very easy switching from a big band to a trio, and so forth, like even getting off of the trio to the big band.
But let's see, where am I with...
We're into the group with Joe Carroll, and playing the libraries and playing the different gigs...
